reviewContext.note: Iteration 5 is a targeted structural re-review of REQ-204's replacement of phrase-enumeration with whole-section-deletion (heading-through-next-heading), per manifest.json's explicit ask to verify the PROP-204a=>PROP-203b entailment by re-reading runtime/loop/prompt.mjs fresh, in full, for ANY ranking language surviving outside the two named sections.

FIND-301.status: RESOLVED for the specific instance named (the '## MINDSET' section is now one of PROP-204a's two named whole-section-deletion targets, and its exact heading-through-next-heading boundary was re-verified against the current file: lines 98-104 inclusive of the trailing blank line before '## Tips').
FIND-301.note: The structural redesign itself (heading-substring absence as a Tier-0 check, replacing phrase-enumeration and 'references/duplicates' reasoning) is a genuine improvement in kind over iterations 3-4's approach and correctly closes the SPECIFIC MINDSET-vs-bootstrap-block scope disagreement FIND-301 raised. However, the redesign's own completeness claim (REQ-204's 'Closed-inventory cross-check') does not hold for the CURRENT file when the check is actually run in full -- see FIND-401.

blockingFindings.summary: REQ-204's 'Closed-inventory cross-check' claims a fresh full re-read of prompt.mjs found no ranking/imperative language outside its closed four-part removal list. This is false: buildUserMessage (a separate, un-examined function in the same file) contains 'Do NOT repeat them now' (a literal, case-insensitive match for PROP-203b's own named grep marker 'do not') plus 'it is FORBIDDEN this wake. Pick a DIFFERENT slot.' -- steering text of equivalent strength to what REQ-204 removes, outside all three of PROP-204a's closed targets, the Tips section, and the yield-bullet adjudication.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: This is the third consecutive iteration (after FIND-201, FIND-301) in which a claimed-complete removal scope is disproven by a genuinely fresh full-file read; PROP-204a's Tier-0 PASS does not structurally imply PROP-203b's PASS for the current file, exactly the entailment this revision was supposed to establish.

blockingFindings.summary: PROP-203b's verification method is a fixed keyword grep, which is under-inclusive by construction (paraphrases like 'FORBIDDEN'/'Pick a DIFFERENT slot', and typographic emphasis like the economy/gig bullet's unique '★THE LABOR MARKET★' star-framing, evade every listed marker word while functioning as the exact steering REQ-203 prohibits).
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: A syntactic keyword-presence check is being used as proof of a semantic absence claim; the two are shown to diverge on the current file, so the verification method cannot certify what REQ-203/REQ-204 actually require.

blockingFindings.summary: REQ-204's Tier-0 check claims self-sufficiency ('no separate check-the-body step') it does not have; it only catches naive heading-only deletions (which orphan the body text elsewhere) because PROP-203b's separate full-file re-scan is relied on as an undocumented dependency.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: A Phase 3 reviewer following REQ-204's own stated self-sufficiency claim could score an incomplete deletion (heading gone, imperative body text still present, orphaned into a neighboring section) as satisfying REQ-204.

convergenceSignals.recommendation: The whole-section-deletion redesign is the right STRUCTURAL direction (Tier-0 heading-boundary checks are more mechanical than phrase-enumeration or 'references/duplicates' reasoning) and should be kept. But this iteration's 'closed-inventory cross-check' claim was written without actually reading buildUserMessage, which is part of the SAME file PROP-203b explicitly scopes itself to ('the FULL current runtime/loop/prompt.mjs'). The next revision must: (1) extend REQ-204's removal/rewording scope to buildUserMessage's 'overuse'/'avoid' diversification steering (prompt.mjs:202-206), naming it as a fourth/fifth closed target the same way the two whole sections and two economy/gig clauses are named, or explicitly and separately adjudicate it out of scope with the same rigor as the yield-bullet edge case; (2) either replace PROP-203b's fixed-keyword-grep method with a semantic/holistic read (consistent with this project's own hard rule that judgment calls belong to the reviewer/model, not a brittle keyword list) or explicitly acknowledge its known blind spots (paraphrase, typographic emphasis) and require a supplementary holistic read; (3) make REQ-204's Tier-0 check explicitly state its dependency on PROP-203b's full-file re-scan rather than claiming standalone sufficiency.
